text:
song: Heads-up — I ran a split-queue experiment this morning: soft fence + separate pools for prefill vs decode. Quick summary: p95 generation latency for short responses (<40 tokens) went up ~18%. CPU/GPU looked fine, but KV hit rate on decode dropped a lot. :thinking:

song: Config we used (excerpt):
```yaml
batching:
  prefill_token_budget: 512
  decode_token_budget: 64
  prefill_pool_size: 6
  decode_pool_size: 2
  fence_mode: soft
kernel:
  affinity: dynamic
handshake:
  timeout_ms: 8
```

song: Profiling (rough):
```
-- decode path --
avg latency: 42ms (was 35ms)
p95: 120ms (was 101ms)
KV cache hit rate (decode): 65% (was 92%)
batch size (decode): median=2, mean=2.3
```

perf-bot: Canary metrics snapshot: GPU util 54%, SM occupancy 27%, scheduler waiting spikes at ~30s intervals, prefill throughput steady, decode Q length microbursts. decode_kv_hits: 65%, prefill_kv_hits: 90%.

maria: @song thanks for the notes. Two quick hypotheses: (1) the soft fence is causing decode requests to lose warm KV entries because prefill batches are being separated and evicting small decode primed keys, (2) dynamic kernel affinity chose a larger kernel for small decode batches which hurts latency.

aj: Agree with maria. We saw small-batch penalties when `affinity: dynamic` picks the fused matmul kernel on <=4 token batches. For decode-solo flows we should force `kernel_affinity: small-kernel` or set a threshold to prefer the low-latency kernel for <8 token batches.

ralph: Also check handshake/handoff ordering. If decode pools are tiny (2) and a prefill handshake holds the worker while it waits on KV drain, short decodes might queue behind it. Can you paste a trace of a slow request?

song: trace snippet (timestamps are ms offsets):
```
[0.0] recv req (decode)
[1.8] enqueue decode Q
[2.1] attempt handshake -> blocked by prefill drain
6.2] handshake completes
[6.3] decode kernel selected: fused-large-kernel
[6.5] exec start
[127.0] send tokens (long tail)
```

maria: That `attempt handshake -> blocked by prefill drain` line is the smoking gun. Two low-effort experiments: (A) bump `decode_pool_size` to 4 and reduce `prefill_pool_size` to 4 so they’re more balanced, (B) reduce `prefill_token_budget` to 256 so prefill batches are smaller and don't evict KV as aggressively.

aj: And toggle kernel affinity override for decode path: `kernel.affinity.decode = small` in our config. Also consider increasing `handshake.timeout_ms` to 12ms so short decodes don't get starved by transient prefill drains.

perf-bot: After an ad-hoc run with `decode_pool_size=4` and `kernel.affinity.decode=small` for 15m: p95 dropped to +3% vs baseline, KV hit rate back to 88% for decode, median decode batch size unchanged.

deploy-bot: Canary deployed: commit c3f9b8a -> toggled `kernel.affinity.decode=small` on canary hosts in us-west-2.

ralph: Nice. If canary holds, we should add a targeted unit test that simulates alternating prefill+decode bursts to catch regressions. Also add a perf regression alert for decode kv_hit_rate <80% and p95 > baseline*1.10.

maria: If we still see tail pain after those steps, fallback plan B is unify queue with phase-aware priority: single pool but with decode priority tokens so decode gets fast-path scheduling while still sharing warmed KV. That lets us avoid cold-KV evictions from strict pool separation.

song: Sounds like a plan. I'll run systematic microbench with: (1) prefill_budget=256, decode_budget=128, (2) increase decode_pool_size to 4, (3) force small kernel for decode, (4) add tracepoints. Will report numbers by EOD. Assigning follow-up to myself. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks. If you need a quick harness, I can rip the burster script from infra and adapt it. :rocket:

song: Please do — that would speed iteration.

aj: Also adding a note to the perf playbook about kernel selection heuristics for small-token decodes.

song: OK closing this check-in for now. Will post final runs and a small PR for config changes. :eyes:
